notes.title: Sunder-Dev Diary #2 - Designing a Collaborative World
notes.content: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/4ebea22293b6e141022be38b6ce18a327d53a1e6.png"][/img][/p][h1]A World Designed for Collaboration[/h1][p]In our last blog, we talked about the inspiration behind [i]Sunderfolk[/i] and how we set out to capture the magic of playing tabletop games with friends. Now, we want to dive deeper into how we designed the game to encourage collaboration, making sure that every player has a role to play. [/p][p][/p][h3]Designing for Collaboration[/h3][p]One of thew ways we help bridge the gap for players new to traditional roleplaying games is through animal characters. For example, someone unfamiliar with RPG archetypes might not fully grasp what a tank does, but if they're playing as a bear character, they might assume it can take a strong hit. This makes the gameplay intuitive while still offering depth for seasoned players. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/71a85d7a08b2c34a21bc7d813670b35eb78b8432.png"][/img][/p][p]At its core, [i]Sunderfolk[/i] is about teamwork. Every hero has strengths and weaknesses, and pulling off the best turn often means working together—whether that's maximizing damage on a tough enemy or ensuring the party's survival through strategic ability use. No hero is good at everything, and that's by design. [/p][p]The challenge—and the fun—comes from analyzing the turn and debating the best approach as a team:[/p][p]-> "What if we try this?"[/p][p]-> "Maybe this ability will help."[/p][p]-> "Oh, I've got something that could make this even better."[/p][p]From the very beginning, we designed the game around these moments, encouraging players to collaborate and problem-solve together. [/p][p][/p][h3]Storytelling with Player Creativity in Mind[/h3][p]This emphasis on collaboration extends to how we tell the game's story. We don't want to give players all of the answers about the world, characters, or NPCs—because that leaves space for your own interpretations and storytelling. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/1357a131fad133e73c4fee8031aeed02c57fa1c4.png"][/img][/p][p]For example, imagine a fire pill bug who has been ostracized by his town. Your band of heroes can show him he's worthy of his duties. These moments—where you and your friends create your own stories within our world—are what make [i]Sunderfolk[/i] special. [/p][p][/p][h1]Translating Tabletop to Video Games[/h1][p]One of our biggest challenges was recreating the [i]physical [/i]experience of playing a board game in a way that felt natural in a digital format. [/p][p]Early iterations of [i]Sunderfolk[/i] experimented with mechanics that felt too detached—like having players rely on personal screens rather than interacting with a shared board. [/p][p]The entire hex grid was replicated on the phone for combat, meaning players spent most of their turn looking down, missing the action and those fun, shared moments. We found that constantly shifting between the phone and the main screen created a "head-bobbing" effect that pulled players out of the experience. That realization led us to completely revamp our control scheme. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/daed4c5672bcfe6911a8c2dcee6caf5564b0918c.png"][/img][/p][p]Through trial and iteration, we landed on the system you see today: [b]a personal screen that acts more like a controller.[/b] This allows players to stay focused on the main screen while using their phone as a cursor, making interactions smoother and more intuitive. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/86f51c74bb796089b140200669e899c98a3f89f9.png"][/img][/p][p]Beyond that, the personal screen helps manage character and inventory interactions without slowing things down for the group. It mirrors the feel of traditional tabletop games, where players have their own character sheets or cards to reference while others take their turns.[/p][p]Our goal? To rekindle excitement for tabletop games—even for those who might be new to the genre. [/p][p][/p][h3]From Closed Beta to Now [/h3][p]One of my favorite parts of the closed beta \[back in 2024] haws been watching players experience the game firsthand—whether they love it, struggle with it, or find something frustrating. Seeing real reactions and knowing that every piece of feedback, positive or critical, helps us imp\[rove has been incredibly rewarding. [/p][p]One of the biggest takeaways has been feedback on the control scheme—some players found it uncomfortable based on how they use the personal screen. We're already exploring alternative options because, at the end of the day, we want as many people as possible to enjoy [i]Sunderfolk. [/i][/p][p]Beyond the feedback itself, one of the most inspiring aspects of the beta has been the community—how supportive and positive players have been towards each other, the dev team, and the game itself. It's not something we take for granted. [i]Sunderfolk is about [/i][b]cooperation[/b], and seeing the community rally around that vision has been amazing. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/8806faa098ae3ff199e4957cfb77d5335211860a.png"][/img][/p][p]Hearing what players have to say and understanding what they want not only improves this game, but also helps shape everything we create in the future. The more we understand our players, the better we can make games for them. [/p][p]So, to everyone's played, shared feedback, and been part of this journey—[b]thank you. [/b]Your input is shaping not just [i]Sunderfolk[/i], but the future of what we create. We can't wait to keep building with you. [/p][list][*][p]Erin Marek, Game Director for Sunderfolk[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Sunderfolk Animation Style Guide
notes.content:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/a37fa3c9d5f66ba5ac4b0c912978087c64738b1c.png"][/img][/p][p]**[i]Gremlin editor's note: This guide features prototype character models. Enjoy the blast from the past AND the learning![/i][/p][p][/p][h1]SUNDERFOLK ANIMATION STYLE GUIDE[/h1][p][i]Author: Alvin Geno
Updated 12/12/2022[/i][/p][p][/p][h2]What is the Sunderfolk Animation Style?[/h2][p]Our animation style is best described as [b]designed[/b] reality. Design is used to describe the hand crafted choices to clarify the [b]timing[/b], [b]posing[/b] and [b]intent[/b] of the choices being made while animating.
[/p][h2]What is unique about our game?[/h2][olist][*][p]We need the poses to clearly show what our character's role is in the game. The character’s overall body language, type of weapon and combat  proficiency (How skilled they are), should be immediately readable from the game camera.[/p][/*][*][p]Our game is turn based  so we must always think about where the player's eye is looking. Use anticipations as a great way to draw the players eye to what's about to happen.[/p][/*][*][p]Our main game camera is fairly far from the characters. We should make sure that our pose changes are large and clear enough to read from far.[/p][/*][*][p]Our characters are fairly detailed so we should always design a focal point. Think of where you want the audience to look the most. Think about a primary, secondary and tertiary read. Always make sure the player does not miss the most important  part of the animation.[/p][/*][*][p]Our game does not rely on quick player control and response. We always know what player state our animation will be transitioning to and from. This means we can author transitions straight into our animation clips where necessary for Polish.[/p][/*][*][p]Our game has many characters. As more characters get animated, always compare new animation content to existing characters to make sure we are not repeating choices.[/p][/*][*][p]Although our characters should be specific. We should leave enough room for the player to  add their own creative input as to what/who/why our character is the way they are.[/p][/*][/olist][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/4730228cdbe283e88781a4b5ad4015fbbdd1412f.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/fa4132b17068fc11a2b8a140c2a96cab237b179b.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/1130c2d373cbc7e70a3288a452cbb0906c30196c.gif"][/img][/p][h2]Sunderfolk Animation Principles:[/h2][olist][*][p][b]Character Specificity[/b][/p][olist][*][p]The character brief will always be your starting point. Always think about how this character would do the specific action. If the choice you make can be put on another character and it still works, you have made the wrong choice.[/p][/*][*][p]Below is an example of a character brief:[/p][p][url="https://miro.com/app/board/uXjVPLVVbOQ=/"]
[/url][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/f34c0fbf61812a582ca4bfdcca462285fd1681c1.png"][/img][/p][/*][/olist][/*][*][p][b]Strong shape design[/b][/p][olist][*][p]We need to pay extra attention to the overall character posing and the shapes being created. This helps make sure we clearly understand what we are looking at from the game camera
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/b74612adb162162a62d614b29e5deab97ea6ea68.png"][/img]1. Clear line of action. This should inform us where the character is coming from and where the character is going.
2. Clear directionality of weapon. We need to define a clear sense of where the character is looking and what they intend to do.[/p][/*][*][p]Make sure to define a very Clear silhouette from all game camera angles.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/23d98f5bdda2c08834d32dbe47702ab2fd58478c.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/db61c8cc312bbda581125ca711a2a2b970efc7b9.png"][/img][/p][/*][*][p]When designing a pose make sure to break up angles of the body so they do not perfectly align with any axis.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/37e1e5096674c1258f711cf0555be529ad1f412a.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/1be4bfd2dbe9f6ec0d5a7bbccd71ea87ba04ed8f.png"][/img][/p][/*][*][p]We must be intentional with character balance. The character weight should feel intentionally distributed. This means they are balanced when they are supposed to be balanced and off balance when intentionally designed to show direction of movement. See Green Lines below
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/4c4491f7c0da5edfb3f95843d3dadabd6ebd46dc.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/50a9df86f21203670b3edaf66ebb2b9ae53abdcb.png"][/img][/p][/*][*][p]We need to Incorporate [b]tilting[/b], Overall [b]rhythm[/b] and [b]twist[/b] throughout our pose design to keep it dynamic.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/c12d57562eda52f60d06fcd6b31b83587c79a8fa.png"][/img][/p][/*][*][p]Each character should be easily associated with a general overall shape. Try and keep this in mind as you define the different poses.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/53bd552b196bb4e22e293931e8b756210b99bf20.png"][/img]Big Hero 6 (2014) [i]Image property of Disney[/i][/p][/*][*][p]We should also think very carefully about the transitional poses between our main core poses. What is commonly referred to as breakdowns or inbetweens. Wherever possible think of simplifying into basic geometric shapes.[/p][olist][*][p]Example from God Of War (2018) [i]Property of Sony Santa Monica Studios.[/i]  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/e048370d32c4c502c40e3b2a709576808347519c.gif"][/img]Nice simple and clear overall shapes that communicate direction. They also communicate an overall sense of force through the squashing and stretching of the overall shape.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/bc124a0822fc505dce752b23e87ecb03c0d06035.gif"][/img]Strong and clear poses make it easy to understand the action despite the character having an overall complex silhouette.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/02006525fc22d2d5ed2149e4fb8f5b20d35e4b9f.gif"][/img][/p][/*][/olist][/*][/olist][/*][*][p][b]Appeal[/b][/p][olist][*][p]Appeal is referring to making choices that when combined make our animation desirable to experience. 
Ask yourself  the following[/p][olist][*][p]Do users want to look at this?[/p][/*][*][p]Does this feel satisfying and impactful?[/p][/*][/olist][/*][*][p]Appeal should be considered both at a single pose basis, and also across frames during the animation. The overall performance should bring delight.
Example:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/5008252d075ef3925d891ac77abf8e36a224a7fd.jpg"][/img]Norman Rockwell’s Proud Professor (1940)[/p][olist][*][p]Norman Rockwell often made many intentional choices to allow his art to bring the most delight to his audience.[/p][/*][/olist][/*][/olist][/*][*][p][b]Clarified timing[/b][/p][olist][*][p]In our Game the timing should be caricatured to support the intent of the character. Make things faster to clarify expertise. Make things slower to suggest stability and/or carefulness. 
Remember, the timing will be specific to each character. 
Some characters are heavy so always ask yourself: [b]How can we use timing to emphasize how heavy they are?[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Contrast:
Make sure to place moments of stillness close to moments of fast motion to better contrast and exaggerate each other. 
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/9ba8fca1a9d94a989ab040d63d654ee6bf77f6de.gif"][/img][/p][/*][*][p]Texture:
Make sure to vary the rhythm and cadence of the animation [b]phrases[/b] to keep the animation  interesting.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/795292f34670593c5e0879dca0ba707a83993923.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/95309c3689dacd92acff71c217645f3f0d3dab90.gif"][/img]A [b]phrase[/b] is a clear movement that supports a single smaller idea within a bigger movement sequence. E.g[/p][olist][*][p]For the Bigger Movement Sequence of Firing an Arrow, the phrases would be:[/p][olist][*][p]The [b]Anticipation[/b] of pulling the bow string[/p][/*][*][p]The [b]Action [/b]of Releasing the string and Firing the Arrow[/p][/*][*][p]The [b]Settle[/b] back into the Ready/Idle pose.
[/p][/*][/olist][/*][/olist][/*][/olist][/*][*][p][b]Physical believability[/b][/p][olist][*][p]Physical believability is[b] not[/b] to be confused with [b]Realism[/b]. We should [b]reference[/b] [b]reality[/b] to inform our choices but [b]caricature and design[/b] our animation to deliver the [b]feeling we want[/b] the user to take away. [/p][olist][*][p]Take an example. In the[b] Attack_SingleArrow[/b] animation for the Ranger. We [b]do not animate[/b] the Ranger removing the arrow from the quill on the Rangers back [b]in a physically correct manner[/b]. 
In fact, We add[b] just enough poses[/b] to communicate that the Ranger is reloading but focus on the[b] smoothness of the timing[/b]. The goal here is to allow the Ranger to look [b]comfortable and efficient[/b] with this motion. Emphasizing the fact that the Ranger has done this countless amount of times.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/20c5a94bd71a9261cbeac1827697f35e36fe6627.gif"][/img]In full speed it is physically believable
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/4730228cdbe283e88781a4b5ad4015fbbdd1412f.gif"][/img][/p][/*][*][p]Also note. In the example above the Ranger shifts weight forward onto the ranger's left foot before being able to lift up the Ranger’s rear foot. This motion is rooted in real physics. Please refer to real life for inspiration when animating our characters.[/p][/*][/olist][/*][/olist][/*][*][p][b]Fluidity and Readability[/b][/p][olist][*][p][b]Fluidity[/b] is all about how our poses change from one frame to another. We should always consider the following  
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/41e58d4537acfcae4ca5d258b204125070bcf45e.gif"][/img][/p][p][b]
FLUID EXAMPLE
[/b][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/02006525fc22d2d5ed2149e4fb8f5b20d35e4b9f.gif"][/img][/p][olist][*][p]Does the next pose clearly flow out of the previous pose?[/p][/*][*][p]Does the pose clearly communicate what the character is doing?[/p][/*][*][p]Is this the Hero pose? If so, what can I do to make sure the audience sees this hero pose clearly?[/p][/*][*][p]How is the overall shape of each of the main body parts flowing from one frame to another? Is the spacing too much?[/p][/*][*][p]What are my focal points and how do I contrast them from other movements to direct the eye of the viewer?
Please note how the draw-overs on the [b]FLUID EXAMPLE[/b] on the right really exaggerate the amount of squash and stretch. This helps with readability from the game camera
[/p][/*][/olist][/*][*][p][b]Fluidity[/b] is also expressed in how the various animation clips flow into each other. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/31729bbf1c0217728e17ad96ae17a8b18bd5cd46.gif"][/img][/p][p][i]Metroid Dread (2021) Property of Nintendo Entertainment[/i][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/660c4773fb8de29097f83fef8567f6d30f8dd83a.gif"][/img]So we should take extra care to make sure to maintain momentum across animation clips. E.g.[/p][olist][*][p]Idle → Walk[/p][/*][*][p]Walk → Ready[/p][/*][*][p]Attack → Ready[/p][/*][*][p]… and more[/p][/*][/olist][/*][*][p][b]Designed Transitional Shapes[/b] are very important. Wherever possible think of designed shapes that flow in and out of each other.  Always preserve the overall volume of the character.  Think about squash and stretch as an animation principle. Exaggerate the squash and stretch to be readable from the game camera[/p][/*][/olist][/*][*][p][b]Fun[/b][/p][olist][*][p]Have fun with the animation. Take all the previous principles. Mix, match and experiment within those expectations. Allow the character description to inspire you to surprise the audience with a unique animation choice. We have characters based on real world animals. Let their unique anatomy and movement inform your choices. [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/7017eb74b25251915d5f505348b4b0097228f41f.gif"][/img][/p][p][i]Moss Book 2 (2022) Above Animation by Laura Ivy Lico. Property of PolyArc. Included for reference purposes only.[/i][/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/102527cce549fea994b1a25b3473ea1b6fb058b6.gif"][/img][/p][/*][*][p]Reference from other animals can inspire fun ways to accomplish animation. Image above could be used to inspire a fun death animation. [i]Courtesy of @viralhog on youtube.[/i] [/p][/*][*][p]Remember to be inspired by other well timed and textured animation [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/52675d9b0a2f5b43cd4f9665055963c37f473596.gif"][/img][/p][/*][*][p][i]Video Courtesy of Pixar Animation Studios. Piper (2016)[/i][/p][/*][/olist][/*][/olist][p][/p][h1]Sunderfolk Animation Process:[/h1][p][b]Game Camera[/b] should be prioritized. In fact, We expect to review the animation from all views in the provided Game Camera Rig.[/p][h2][b] 1. Pose Exploration[/b][/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/89a00793a3c8a6500aa330663f3cb8a6903cd8a4.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/b543de9b3fbd17d9ed32f7f3a53bba2983686dcf.png"][/img][i]Image courtesy of Alvin Geno. Warcraft Arclight Rumble (2022)[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/30591d70a8caf396436a07fdebf8066d8a3849f7.jpg"][/img][i]Image courtesy of Steve Hendershot. Undisputed Street Fighter: A 30th Anniversary Retrospective[/i][/p][p]
At the beginning of every new [b]character exploration[/b] is [b]pose exploration[/b]. It's the most important part of the process.[/p][p]
The goal here is to [b]quickly iterate and experiment with poses[/b] to learn what works and what doesn’t work for our character.[/p][p]
The quick iteration allows us to [b]quickly get feedback[/b] and see what this looks like.
[b]Please note: [/b]This is also a good time to show video reference. However, the video reference will not be used as ground truth because we will only commit to ideas that have been illustrated on the character rig.[b]
[/b][/p][olist][*][p]Most important thing is the character brief. Refer to it often to inform the choices you make with the character.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/f34c0fbf61812a582ca4bfdcca462285fd1681c1.png"][/img]Though there is no limit to what kind of poses an animator can explore. It’s important for the animator to experiment with poses that will inform the animation clips we intend to create.
In this case… Idles, Attacks, Walks, Fidgets, knockdowns…e.t.c.[/p][olist][*][p]At this stage it is important to gather as [b]much reference [/b]as possible to make your choices [b]as specific as possible[/b].[/p][/*][/olist][/*][*][p]All the pose explorations should be in a single Maya file.[/p][/*][/olist][h2]
2. [b]Animation Blockout[/b][/h2][p]The goal here is to [b]build upon the feedback[/b] from the pose exploration phase to [b]clearly describe[/b] what the animation will look like in the most efficient way possible.[/p][p]
We expect a clear breakdown of the following[/p][p][/p][olist][*][p][b]Step 1: Core Poses
[/b]Core Poses are the images we want the player to remember the most from the animation clip. These should really capture the personality of the character. They should build upon the [url="https://docs.google.com/document/d/15PdW9jc3-HHsG6_jXVgQpLggdc5a1Rf79YXqXJ0x2Dk/edit#heading=h.q3hbflff0qdm"][u]strong shape design[/u][/url] principle.  
[/p][p]Examples: Ranger_Base_Attack_SingleArrow (4 poses) [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/1019df24de6a7c9ea0d9c894e9b4b94aed980dc9.gif"][/img]Ranger_Base_DamageFront (4 poses) [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/736a68d46dc3845e1ff5784b3339641f2a720cc2.gif"][/img]Ranger_Base_Attack_ArrowBarrage (4 poses) 
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/d6b70f32c615507403fda6d2e58f50ec33a08f75.gif"][/img][/p][p align="center"]
~End of Core Pose examples~[/p][/*][*][p][b]Step 2: Transition Poses[/b]
These clearly describe how we get in and out of the core poses. These poses will help describe the physical believability of the character.
Timing Should be clearly defined. We want to get as much of a sense of the intended impact as clearly as possible.

[b]Examples:[/b]

notes.title: Design-a-Mission Update #1 - Setting The Stage
notes.content:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/1917942b9a02517e5b7beb40b2fdb2508845f534.png"][/img][/p][p]Hey Guardians![/p][p][/p][p]You voted and our design team heard! The community collab mission has been underway for a few weeks now, and we’re pretty pleased with the progress. We’ll be updating everyone on the process for creating this event, starting… NOW! [/p][p][/p][p]As a refresher, here’s the criteria that our amazing community voted for:  [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/f275720442b3d2931a138f73ba104c17a0a70e56.png"][/img][/p][p align="center"][i]THIS IS WHAT YOU ASKED FOR[/i]
[/p][p]Once we had the final votes for everything, we shipped them off to our design team, who immediately got to work! [/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcdKcuZ0PATRGJIL50QW46TszecHMvy7LLC6iknbV_wF8-VkcnH2R5w5TK4u0jg-goeM18XkL3SQOJ_Uyo9RRjJa8-B-F9bCpd-bpXOz657w_PQrxfne6wCunAVrdTvSWOTNqT3dA?key=CCCWi4Xpikrpv-d0J5beXA"][/img][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeVCsb2xqdrrhDnU7YQS7j0nzqfY2HeDHG8At56ypJenWzU7TVc7E7tcwtds4sbgW8aPqrnJtxX4zLmJcmgHCP1S2u5VCiPK50xyLl8Qjwpz00EGxlGClzACT9o2HljmlIX4Du8qA?key=CCCWi4Xpikrpv-d0J5beXA"][/img][/p][p align="center"][i]Game design[/i]
[/p][p]Then after that is picking the best map that matches the gameplay, and of course, what our community voted for![/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfFz36XwAl7HBvuEmL9j-jVgSvovB8MaAt2z5FkJcrzso2qBBVeZQjoYWuFN10ipgPfFrzmxHzb4VAn4WlC8C__XPHgUA9S8zarGHavzUnGtdi19r0XCdr5sQi6Ygs_2BvNmrMqfQ?key=CCCWi4Xpikrpv-d0J5beXA"][/img][/p][p align="center"][i]One of theeeeese is the final winner! Can you guess which one it is? [/i][/p][p][/p][p]After some thinking, light touches of creativity, and design madness, the concept begins to form: [/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdAx3VaIYQDT17F0gz0MorXUD2myUPJNP6UDmyFzmV78wXAOwD2Ff--c35vqMFkUysyGEYIBFk7uNG1lj_kg8K4bf-QG-lpuWQnqXD8rXeW0hOg4IabASXXGE8l7nGXHu51cIibGA?key=CCCWi4Xpikrpv-d0J5beXA"][/img][/p][p align="center"][i]Memes are vital to the design process. [/i]
[/p][p]After some more brainstorming and iteration, a gameplay loop forms, and with that, a mission begins its first steps into the world. 
[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd9LW5LnllaW60NNOT0GABU2zchSUEo1GSLYW78HMPIbUENqLOq0umhDY4-0lELIEfq-xc0mj54oZwPfDozFp8rQwvb5kkLQdSsnF7dyu6QjS2xy4Cgy911MQunu2SdZIBfe5XouQ?key=CCCWi4Xpikrpv-d0J5beXA"][/img][/p][p align="center"][i]Button Mushroom decided to block the level reveal. The little rascal! [/i]
[/p][p]Stay tuned for our next update where we’ll reveal the map and the mission name! That’s right, the community voted for the name too! You can see the results of that on our [url="http://discord.gg/sunderfolk"][u]Discord[/u][/url]! 
[/p][p]If you simply can’t wait for the community mission reveal and you happen to be attending PAX West this year, we HIGHLY recommend stopping by! You might just be able to have your wish fulfilled. <3[/p][p][/p][p]We’ll see you soon, Guardians! [/p][list][*][p]The Sunderfolk Team[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Sunderfolk Update #4 - 1.4.1 Hotfix Notes
notes.content: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/59c9beaf8903e53da323830dee189bb0686fe703.png"][/img][/p][p]Hello Guardians! [/p][p][/p][p]We’ve been hard at work on fixing disconnection issues that have been affecting some Sunderfolk players, and we’re excited to have a fix for our Guardians. [/p][p][/p][h3]Hotfix 1.4.1[/h3][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where some players would experience frequent disconnections between the Sunderfolk main screen and phone controller app. [/p][list][*][p]This particular issue was caused by some firewalls dropping a required server connection due to limited network activity over the connection. This disconnect would most likely have been experienced while playing remotely over the Internet. The game now handles this situation better.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]Please note, this hotfix may not prevent every possible network disconnection issue, and we always appreciate your feedback and reports for finding and squashing bugs.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you![/p][list][*][p]The Sunderfolk Team[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Sunderfolk Update #3 - 1.4 Patch Notes & Summary
notes.content:
[p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXewDjKumDYkqNBSSfuC1uI75GPls-KFOc9A_UESdJ4XawtYkMPqRUReoq9oCZVMxx-Kd69Y3ss9fuH6C0MVuNTc8URepaCybOlUGKpGposXPhiozDbMsuhj5078KQOVcc9HDiYtSg?key=dXOucwgLmqQ9mGthZxm1kLxP"][/img][/p][p][i]We discovered that you can, in fact, make a salad too powerful. Image credit to Discord user SilentBob4207. [/i][/p][p][/p][p]Hey Guardians![/p][p]You’ve spoken, and we’ve heard! We’ve been collecting your feedback and seeing where Sunderfolk shines and where it needs polish.
[/p][p]This latest patch focuses on some popular community requests, as well as an expressive new feature.😁 [/p][p][/p][h2]What’s New / Priority Fixes in Sunderfolk [/h2][p][b]Now introducing: Emotes[/b][/p][p]Players can now use Sunderfolk emotes with customizable text during combat and in-town. [/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeazcNiQ6OhmRBs7WFEmycE-Ud4Yeu99CGI-YgVNpgwAQR-Eh2rNnnkrISZ6D9HzdgdzPAP76nGdmNOY4QtBkTVDZ_H2L_hrwLfTqILBkFVmtbv6h-W0qSjM3wcApzrrERn_MvYbQ?key=dXOucwgLmqQ9mGthZxm1kLxP"][/img] [i]Just click the Smile icon and go nuts! This will appear in town and during missions! [/i][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf5GPiX2JiHenkpt6U3IyK0UkWriAPWcF37zRZUBds1OkoTuwR_rtLyJ0iDoGTqh7B4zEBNgaPbDY1bY_Rz_PukHxWWDZ0OPW2PRWIpyhN32R8C0NAzKm-O11AB-phW5uEzQm1s?key=dXOucwgLmqQ9mGthZxm1kLxP"][/img][/p][list][*][p][b]Renameable Player Prompts[/b][/p][list][*][p]Were you too much of a [u][url="https://www.penny-arcade.com/comic/2025/04/30/we-create-worlds"]loremaster [/url][/u]and now you have to show your campaign to your family? We’ve got your back! Players can now rename the in-game prompts through the Shared Settings menu. [/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfvWy99FMDWhDXyxv61AUBHvdY0IArUgEhKDDO50qDovWchj98BWGW3SBj9wOPn5nxCFdDdUTM3NyuGH7fCW-jh4lYE_WAtg2qVvgMxQtvjL_462N-wuzkX4k3qLMRWZHqlxKA3eQ?key=dXOucwgLmqQ9mGthZxm1kLxP"][/img][/p][p][b]Name/Rename Your Campaign[/b][/p][list][*][p]Players will now be able to name their campaign party as part of the Hero Select process, which will be used as the Save File name. [/p][/*][*][p]Players may change their party name later via the Shared Settings menu. [/p][list][*][p]For players already in existing campaigns, you can create a new name for your party through Settings -> Shared Settings -> Campaign Rename. [/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfAphr_7ylUNILu1MljdBu0m52RLmmk26Te_iRiPMc1uysEDrysUBpgf9qWjD-9wSFz3y0HwQbgntZ6O5FEBg4gRbnEuGpyWFxNhgvtqe1bad-OhcWRziyNiIfH3jbjKt9O0b17DA?key=dXOucwgLmqQ9mGthZxm1kLxP"][/img][/p][p][b]Adjusted Boss Difficulty for Challenging/Shadowstone[/b][/p][list][*][p]Boss monsters now receive a +1 damage buff like other monsters, instead of the unique +2 damage buff previously used. [/p][/*][/list][p][b]Nerfed the Salad[/b][/p][list][*][p]The Tangleroot Salad has been adjusted to prevent excessive creation of Vines. [/p][/*][*][p]The flavor text description for Tangleroot We’re focusing on bug fixes, bringing some quality of life additions, and little doses of love![/p][p][/p][p][i][b]Please note: The update will be released across all platforms simultaneously, but due to platform differences, you may see the update available for download at different times. We expect the update to be available to all players (across all platforms) within 30 minutes of patch release time. All platforms will receive the update by 10AM PDT / 1PM EDT / 17:00 UTC.[/b][/i][/p][p][/p][h2]What’s New / Priority Fixes in Sunderfolk [/h2][p][b]Timestamps on Last Saved Campaign [/b][/p][list][*][p]The Campaign screen will now display the time when it was last auto-saved for the active campaign. [/p][/*][/list][p][b]Main Screen Player Prompt[/b][/p][list][*][p]The main screen now shows whose personal screen needs to respond before it can proceed. [/p][/*][/list][p][b]Auto-Save Notice[/b][/p][list][*][p]An Auto save notice will now appear on Game Start[/p][/*][/list][p][b]New VFX[/b][/p][list][*][p]New visual effects have been added for the following:[/p][list][*][p]Spider Webs[/p][/*][*][p]Redcap Spawners[/p][/*][*][p]Rubble[/p][/*][*][p]The Mimic Shrine[/p][/*][*][p]Minecart[/p][/*][*][p]The “Charge” ability[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][b]Mission Balance Change[/b][/p][list][*][p](This is a story-spoiler: Read at your own risk) Adjusted the enemy spawns for 2-3 player games in the mission \[spoiler]Caravan Protectors, Dead of Night Pt. 1.\[/spoiler][/p][/*][/list][p][b]Smithy Tier 4 Upgrade Fix[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where upgrading the Smithy to Tier 4 was not rewarding players with the additional Skill Card slot. [/p][/*][/list][p][b]Device Disconnections[/b][/p][list][*][p]Reduced the frequency of disconnections under certain remote play situations.[/p][list][*][p][i]Please note: While most players who experienced these problems should see less disconnections, we are still actively investigating further improvements related to connection reliability and for players unable to reconnect via QR code after being disconnected in a future patch. [/i][/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h3][b]Upcoming June 17th[/b][/h3][p][b]The Sunderfolk Free Trial[/b][/p][list][*][p]Play the first 3 tutorial missions and one Act 1 mission during the trial. notes.title: Steam 暂停中国区销售，致力于提升用户体验
notes.content:
[p]在《Sunderfolk》上线后的前五周，我们收到了来自中国玩家的反馈，部分玩家表示自己在游玩本游戏时遇到了一些问题。这些问题包括：未在共同 Wi-Fi 下与好友游玩时出现的连接问题，以及下载安卓版《Sunderfolk》控制器程序时遇到的困难。我们仔细研究了具体问题后，意识到本游戏目前在中国地区的体验尚未达到预期的质量水平。 [/p][p]
[/p][p]我们探讨了多种改善体验的方案，但所有的方案都无法尽快解决问题。因此，我们做出了艰难的决定：在 Steam 平台的中国地区暂时停止销售，然后研究长期解决方案，改善该地区所有玩家的游戏体验。[/p][p]
[/p][p]已经购买游戏的玩家仍可继续游玩。我们还会继续通过 Steam 发布更新和补丁，也会继续更新中文文本。此外，我们已与 UU 加速器达成合作，该加速器可以免费支持游玩《Sunderfolk》，使用 Steam 版本以及连接控制器APP时，能显著改善玩家的联机体验。我们会继续探索改善中国玩家体验的方法，让大家与其他地区的玩家享受一样的游戏乐趣。[/p][p]
[/p][p]非常感谢大家的支持，我们期待尽快解决这些问题，然后在 Steam 中国地区恢复销售。[/p][p][/p][p]===[/p][h2][/h2][h2][b]Steam Sales Paused in China as We Work to Improve Experience[/b][/h2][p][/p][h3]We're investigating long-term solutions for connectivity and access issues in the China region.[/h3][p][/p][p][i]Sales in China are paused while we work on lasting fixes. Current players can keep playing, with updates, support, and UUBooster connectivity improvements ongoing.[/i][/p][p]
[/p][p]After the first five weeks of Sunderfolk's launch, we've heard feedback from players in China indicating that some have experienced issues when playing the game. This includes connectivity problems when not playing on local Wi-Fi and challenges accessing the Android version of the Sunderfolk controller mobile app. After taking a close look at the specific issues, we realize that the experience in China does not currently measure up to the level of quality we strive to achieve for our players. [/p][p]
[/p][p]We explored several options to improve the experience but none offered a quick solution. Because of this, we've made the difficult decision to temporarily suspend Steam sales in China while we investigate long-term solutions to improve the experience for all players within the region.[/p][p]
[/p][p]Existing players that have already purchased the game will continue to be able to play. We will continue to release updates and patches via Steam, and will continue to support Chinese as a language. Additionally, we've managed to secure UUBooster support for Sunderfolk which can greatly improve the connectivity experience for players when used with the Steam version as well as on connecting controllers. We will continue investigating ways to improve the experience for players in China to match other regions.[/p][p]
[/p][p]We greatly appreciate your support and look forward to turning on Steam sales in China as soon as these issues have been addressed.[/p]

notes.title: Beginner's Guide to Sunderfolk
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/36671f4e85e714db1e625630b7f99c84f01a0e85.png[/img]
Hey Guardians! Are you ready to jump into Sunderfolk?

No? Well good thing you stopped by here first!

Here you’ll find everything you need to know to get ready to leap into the Sunderlands and save Arden! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/25746a42fbd31c99f7f62bfb7a11cb490ddde7ea.jpg[/img]
[i]YES, "LEAP" WAS LITERAL[/i]

[h2]Starting Your Campaign[/h2]
Once you’ve chosen your friends to party with you (or are undertaking this adventure solo) you’ll start up Sunderfolk, and create a new campaign by scanning the QR code shown with your Sunderfolk Controller App! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/e2fb24f851d6135ff8ade7826eb5e67236ff5f7e.png[/img]

[i][b]Tip:[/b] Playing remotely with friends and need some help? Check out our handy Remote Guide for those Sunder-friends who are physically apart! [/i]

Once everyone has connected to the game by scanning their phone or tablet with the Controller App, then you’re ready to watch the intro cutscene and begin your Sunderfolk journey! 

[h2]Choose Your Character [/h2]
The playable characters of Sunderfolk have many titles, but they all share the same mission—to protect the townsfolk of Arden. There are six different characters to choose from, all with their own unique playstyle that fills a vital role within a party. 

[list]
[*] [b]The Arcanist[/b] - Master the intricacies of the arcane!
[*] [b]The Bard[/b] - Inspire and deceive with MUSIC!
[*] [b]The Berserker[/b] - Channel your Rage and demolish foes!
[*] [b]The Pyromancer[/b] - Engulf everything in red-hot flames!
[*] [b]The Ranger[/b] - Hunt your opponent from a distance!
[*] [b]The Rogue[/b] - Devastate prey with devious attacks!
[/list]
[i][b]Tip:[/b] Need a thorough guide on all of the heroes before making your decision? Don’t worry, we’ve got you covered! [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/57973e55117b3cfb8e877be4d6c29a72034202ff.png[/img]
[i]Dibs on the Pyromancer![/i]

[h2]Combat in Sunderfolk[/h2]
Sunderfolk utilizes party turn-based, strategy combat separated into Rounds. Each Round of combat encompasses:
[list]
[*] [b]Character Turn[/b] - You and your party members take their turns
[*] [b]Monster Turn[/b] - Your foes take their actions 
[*] [b]Ally Turn[/b] - If you have NPC allies, they’ll act here
[/list]
There are no turn orders for your and your party, allowing for flexibility in your strategies! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/db8c3b7165c5a29db0ac4ded319ffe9d2f0317b1.jpg[/img]
[i]Though we do recommend making sure the Berserker takes all the damage. [/i]

[h2]We’ve Put a Hex On You(r grid)[/h2]

As you may have noticed above, Sunderfolk utilizes a hexagonal grid for the battlefield! This opens up a lot of possibilities, namely for the term “adjacent”! You’ll see that a lot in your character Skill Cards! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/07b474f5fc9215a048c5dc82414e885493a192d1.jpg[/img]
[i]Drop YOUR favorite grid-shape system in the comments below![/i]

An enemy (or ally) can be adjacent to you as long as the hex tile that they are on is touching your hex tile! 

These tiles can also have environmental hazards (sometimes caused by party members), and some are baked into the map itself! 

Tip: When you move, each hex tile counts as one movement! Pushing an enemy or swapping with an ally also counts as one movement. 

[h2]Mission Guide[/h2]
Once you’re in a Mission, you can view your character Skill Cards, passives, equipped items, and remaining Fate Cards all in one place! The guide will also show enemy abilities, their own Skill Cards, and any environmental hazards such as Lava and Slime! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/f77272c04820584367cd494b9108b03cc620bf3d.png[/img]
[i]Who needs memorizing rules and passives when it’s all in front of you? [/i]

[h2]Town and Upgrades[/h2]
The town of Arden is where our heroes reside, and your main focus is to defend it from forces that seek to destroy it. However, within its walls await colorful residents who are happy to provide services and conversation! Think of it as your refuge in-between combat missions. 

Once in town, you’ll be able to: 
[list]
[*] Befriend and deepen relationships with the townsfolk. 
[*] Rebuild and upgrade Buildings. 
[*] Craft and purchase equipment.
[/list]
Each building you rebuild and upgrade will offer a new bonus for your adventuring needs! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/6a2331b0a94508fce44682c21cade38863a0f9d5.png[/img]
[h2]Equipment [/h2]
Equipment in Sunderfolk is focused between 3 core types:

[h3]Trinkets[/h3]
[list]
[*] Trinkets offer extra boosts for combat. They range from dealing damage to nearby foes, buffing, or even healing you. 
[*] You can earn Trinkets by looting them after they’re dropped by defeated enemies, crafted in the Workshop, or purchased in the Market. 
[*] The Workshop must be built in order to craft and upgrade Trinkets. 
[/list]
[h3]Meals[/h3]
[list]
[*] Meals offer extra buffs for combat missions, such as gaining 1 Shield buff if you end your turn next to an ally. 
[*] You can purchase Meals at Sinclair’s Tavern once it’s rebuilt. 
[*] The menu will change each time a Mission is completed, so don’t expect the same one each time. 
[/list]
[h3]Weapons[/h3]
[list]
[*] Weapons are powerful tools that you receive once you’ve leveled up and rebuilt the Smithy. 
[*] Weapons can only be activated after completing their “Energize” requirement. These can range from dealing a certain amount of damage or having an ally take damage near you. 
[*] Weapons can offer different options for your build, such as giving you an extra movement if you complete their Energize requirement. 
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/3ea9e398700937acde9b5b27672fb84fbd8401cf.png[/img]

Once you’re equipped with your gear, you can take on any challenge in the Sunderlands! 

Now you’re geared, equipped, and ready for an adventure! Have more questions? Ask away in the comments below!

The Sunderfolk Team

[*] Ally attacks will no longer trigger enemies’ Frenzy passive in Challenging or Shadowstone difficulty.

[*] [This is a story-spoiler: Read at your own risk] [spoiler]Fixed an issue where a Round Timer is missing in (“All That Glitters”), causing the missions to be blocked from progressing. [/spoiler]

[list]
[*] [This is a story-spoiler: Read at your own risk] [spoiler]Fixed an issue where Heroes would lose more than the intended one Skill Card when deselecting a Skill Card while under the effects of “Fear”.[/spoiler]

[*] Fixed missing and broken audio events in-game. 
[*] Adjusted the description for the “Black Inkwell” trinket to match its functionality. 
[*] [This is a story-spoiler: Read at your own risk] [spoiler]The mission (“Sundered Shadows”) will be reset to start from the beginning if it was saved and players quit in-progress.* [/spoiler]
[/list]
[i]*[b]Developer Note:[/b] Some patches for Sunderfolk may reset the specific mission you are on at the time of the update, if we’ve made changes to how that specific mission works. This will send you back to town, but it will improve your overall experience with the mission. We’ll aim to give more advanced notice if these resets are coming in future patches. Thanks for rolling with it![/i] 🎲

Don’t see an issue you reported? Don’t worry, this is just the beginning of our upcoming patches, so stay tuned!

Thanks for playing Sunderfolk! 

The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: SunderBlog: Guide to Remote Play
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/0a433bd9d87d24c70b75f0afc8292ae5cae63d02.png[/img]

[h2]Entering The Sunderlands… Together[/h2]

While Sunderfolk has been crafted as a couch co-op experience, we all have friends that live in different parts of the world, and we’re looking to close that gap… digitally, at least. 

If you have a group ready to go but are unable to traverse time and space to play together, never fear! Playing Sunderfolk is only a few steps away! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/20b86ffc3c3c900b899ae3f574697839ecab443a.jpg[/img]
[i]This could be us but you’re playing… from very far away. [/i]

[h2]Steam Remote Play[/h2]

To Host Sunderfolk with up to 3 friends via Steam Remote Play: 

[olist]
[*] Add your party members as Steam friends (if you don’t have them already) through the Steam client or through [url=http://steamcommunity.com/my/friends]here[/url]!
[*] Launch Sunderfolk through Steam
[*] Shift-tab to bring up the Steam overlay

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/6e9118b7d56704fcdb46a7afec06be30937fbf0c.png[/img]

[*] Open your friends list and right-click on your party member’s name

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/899dc151cbeb62946a51fe6a79f8e3cc73fffb44.png[/img]

[*] Select “Remote Play Together”, then invite them to your game
[*] Your players will be able to join after accepting the invite on Steam!
[/olist]
Now, all your friends can watch your stream while playing along from their phones. The best part is, they don't need to own the game or even download it to play cooperatively! All they’ll need to do is download the app on iOS or Android and accept your invite, and scan the QR code to join the party!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/110857c53a0c76c191739da4c9a7b8aab6db7cfe.jpg[/img]

[h2]Playing on Discord[/h2]

If you want to spam all of your Discord Nitro emojis while playing, you can also play Sunderfolk remotely with friends through Discord!

To stream Sunderfolk on Discord:
[olist]
[*] Start up “Sunderfolk” on Steam 
[*] Create / Join a Voice Channel (or a private DM call)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/a207272ca52c1bf7de57bb38785ab1d50994f573.png[/img]

[*] When in the voice channel, select “Screen Share” from the options on the bottom-left

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/c21c9416de3eb16fb701794450f02ad664f1195a.png[/img]

[*] On the “Applications” tab, select “Sunderfolk”. Make sure application noises are toggled on so your players can hear the in-game sounds. 
[*] Hit “Go Live” and stream the game to your friends!
[/olist]
Hot Tip: If you join our [url=discord.gg/sunderfolk]Discord server[/url], you’ll be able to join a “looking for group” channel to meet new friends and form a  new adventuring party! 

We’ll see you in the Sunderlands on April 23, 2025! 

The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Sunderfolk - From Closed Beta to Launch
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/b66f4bcba3d0d6b4e4d6058ed0b7acf4554f7671.png[/img]

Hey Guardians!

Our Closed Beta officially ended on February 4th, 2025, after a month and a half of testing! 

During that time, we’ve received over[b] 1200 [/b]feedback submissions, and had [b]1700+ [/b]members join us in our closed beta Discord server! 

Now, we’ve used that information to make Sunderfolk even better and ready for release! Check out some of the upcoming changes in store for launch day, and join us in counting down the big day!

[h1]Some Implemented Changes: [/h1]

[h3]Pacing[/h3]

[i]Many small changes that add up to a major impact on the speed of play. These changes help to streamline the pacing of gameplay: [/i]
[list]
[*] Pulsing animation on the tile of Heroes that haven’t played yet this turn. Hurry up and take your turn!
[*] Movement and attack animations speed up when multiple monsters of the same type take their turns sequentially. This resets when a new monster type takes its turn.
[*] Increased the move and attack animation speed of most characters.
[*] Improvements to missions and Monsters to increase pacing:
[/list]
[olist]
[*] [b]Tower Defense:[/b] Stun Bug now only attacks 1 target, not 3.
[*] [b]Minecart Mayhem:[/b] reduced number of webs.
[*] [b]Lost in Swamp:[/b] re-arranged starting Oozes, increase NPC health.
[*] [b]Oozes’ Fate Cards[/b] no longer spawn additional Oozlings.
[*] [b]The Fungal Vale:[/b] changed Oozes to Redcaps.
[*] [b]Shadowshard: [/b]moved barrels closer to teleporters.
[/olist]

[h3]Settings[/h3]

[i]Added more settings to allow you to remove UI and Narrative friction:[/i]
[list]
[*] Setting to let you [b]Auto-Skip Narrative, Tutorials, and/or Cinematics.[/b]
[*] Setting to let you [b]Auto-End [/b]your turn instead of needing to press the End Turn button.
[*] Added more configuration options for the[b] “Hold to Skip” [/b]feature, allowing you to skip your actions without looking down at your phone.
[*] Added [b]Exit to Hero Select [/b]to make it easier to add new Heroes to existing campaigns.
[/list]

[h3]Difficulty[/h3]

[i]Improving the Difficulty curve to be more consistent across missions, while pushing to distinguish Brightstone and Challenging as more distinct difficulty modes. [/i]
[list]
[*] Easier Brightstone Difficulty mode.
[*] Invincible NPCs.
[*] Harder Challenging Difficulty mode.
[*] All Monsters have Frenzy and become more powerful when they are:
[*] Attacked by a Hero.
[*] Unable to attack for the round.
[*] Stronger Monsters.
[*] More Elite Monsters Spawns.
[*] [b]Shadowstone Difficulty Unlocked Automatically.[/b]
[/list]

[h3]Heroes[/h3]
[i]After analyzing data and going through your feedback, we've made some balance changes to some Heroes![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/2a0658cae46cf42fae40dc6106b80944dd98ef49.png[/img]
[i][b]Arcanist[/b][/i]
[list]
[*] Arcanist is in a good spot; they've received balance tweaks to some spells.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/865387eb18e6de41fed96c59819224646a5d09d1.png[/img]
[i][b]Bard[/b][/i]
[list]
[*] Bard has some room for some extra power, so they received some damage and movement increases.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/ce2b503b03ec08635e8ba38d5709edfb3942ef49.png[/img]
[i][b]Berserker[/b][/i]
[list]
[*] Berserker's in a good spot; touching up some under-loved spells.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/ed20bb20e4c58e20970dd3bab51d7fa4bcb9556a.png[/img]
[i][b]Pyromancer[/b][/i]
[list]
[*] Pyro has a lot of power, so shifting some of that power around.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/94d3483028574135c386f69930658eb4bb51d238.png[/img]
[i][b]Ranger[/b][/i]
[list]
[*] Ranger has some room for some more power; they received some upgrades.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/f370040ccded15795edbf268fd90e11f8a2e6522.png[/img]
[i][b]Rogue[/b][/i]
[list]
[*] Rogue is in a good spot; made some changes to reduce player confusion.
[/list]

[h3]Town[/h3]
[list]
[*] Re-organized building upgrade rewards to more closely match the building theme.
[*] Added a new [b]Market Shop[/b] that exchanges [b]Favors[/b] for certain [b]Trinkets [/b]to create an outlet for excess [b]Favor [/b]items.
[*] Rewrote and added extra text to better describe certain building upgrade rewards.
[*] [b]Level-Up celebration [/b]now happens soon as you arrive at Level-Up.
[*] [b]Tavern Meals[/b] are now weighted, making it more likely newer unlocked / better meals are more likely to appear.
[/list]

[h3]UI/UX[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added a [b]skip remainder of turn[/b] button in combat when taking your turn
[*] Implemented corner cutting on movement & targeting to help improve the ease of drawing your path
[*] Improved tablet UI support
[*] Better telegraphing for unique mission mechanics and rules (story spoilers below!):
[/list]
[olist]
[*] Show which card is Feared in [spoiler] Shadow of Doubt mission. [/spoiler]
[*] Visual status effect for [spoiler] Ritual Healing Water Carrier and Fungal Friends Fungi alignment.[/spoiler]
[/olist]

[h3]Other [/h3]
[list]
[*] Improvements to disconnect handling and flow
[*] Removed the QR code which blocked too much of the screen when players disconnected
[*] More places where the game saves in Town
[*] Added in slide animations when stepping on Slime
[*] Lots of improved VFX, animation, and audio!
[/list]

[h2]Just The Sunder-Start[/h2]

Now, these are just some of the changes we’ve made for launch, and this is just the beginning! If you don’t see your feedback implemented here, we are planning post-launch patches that will include changes that we couldn’t add for our launch day. 

Thank you all again for your feedback, bug reports, and for joining us on this first step into Sunderfolk’s journey! We can’t wait to show you everything! 

[list]
[*] The Sunderfolk Team
[/list]

notes.title: Sunder-Dev Diary #1 - The Inspiration Behind Sunderfolk
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/0a433bd9d87d24c70b75f0afc8292ae5cae63d02.png[/img]

Hi, I’m Erin Marek, Game Director on Sunderfolk. Since kicking off our closed beta back in December, we’ve been blown away by all the great feedback and questions in Discord.

These discussions inspired the team and me to share some insight into our approach to the game. Over the coming weeks, we’ll share some unique perspectives on our different disciplines, backgrounds, and how it all comes together to make Sunderfolk into a game we hope you, your friends, and your family will love. 

To kick off these developer diaries, I’d like to dive into the early development of the game and some of the things we hope to accomplish through Sunderfolk. 

Let’s rewind a bit to some of the earliest conversations around the game.

[h3]Kindling connection with familiarity [/h3]
When the team first started forming the initial concept of the game, one thing kept resurfacing again and again– how much we love the feeling of being together and playing tabletop board games with our friends and family. We set out to build something that inspired those same feelings through a video game experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/b0ac5eac0b3c6db04f93b6bcd731bf2599843f9f.jpg[/img]
[i]Early concept art for Sunderfolk[/i]

At the time of those early brainstorms, Covid had made many of us feel isolated and alone, so there was a really strong desire to find a way to reconnect with those earlier days of just having fun together around the table or in couch co-op. The team started jamming on how we might create similar experiences through video games to make it a little easier for folks who aren’t as familiar with the genre. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/2f7654c681fe91b57b4c5c126d1b9d233fa4cc5e.jpg[/img]
[i]Early pen & paper concept for Sunderfolk combat. See anything familiar?[/i]

[h3]Brightstone versus Shadowstone[/h3]
With the goal of bringing folks together, it was super important for us to make the world around Sunderfolk approachable and inviting for a wide audience. We aimed to strike balance between creating a lighthearted, whimsical world while still allowing for moments of depth and seriousness. 

Our world is shaped by its underground setting, which heavily influenced the game’s themes and design. You’ll see plenty of bugs, mushrooms, stones, gems—elements that bring the environment to life. The overall story itself is another way we think about inviting players in, both novice and veteran. 

A lot of fantasy stories revolve around a classic good-versus-evil dynamic, which is something we really liked because it’s instantly familiar and easy to grasp. This backdrop naturally influenced our take on the good-versus-evil theme, leading us to the central conflict of Brightstone versus Shadowstone.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/3f55d8b8ff94bd0920e4e6c895effce07cb5a2a0.jpg[/img]
[i]Early concept art for the town of Arden[/i]

What we’d really love for folks to take away after they play Sunderfolk is excitement to play more board games and D&D and tabletop games, especially new folks who maybe haven’t played those kinds of games before. 

For groups who have struggled to find the right game to play because it can be exhausting to set up a board game or for a GM to get content ready, we’re hoping that Sunderfolk can help reinvigorate their passion for revisiting those games.

I appreciate you all for taking the time to read this first developer diary! The next focus will be on how Sunderfolk was designed around collaboration and teamwork.

[list]
[*] Erin Marek, Game Director
[/list]
