notes.title: Meet Your Heroes: The Rogue
notes.content:
[h2]Mustelidae Miscreant [/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/47debedb9af3fafdde78e7f5756525f214ab47a8.png[/img]

[i]“If it isn’t my favorite"hero"! I bet you never thought you’d be called that. I know I didn’t!" [/i]- Sinclair, Tavern owner. 

The Rogue may look like they’ll stab you in the back for some loose change, and they may have at some point, but they are devoted to keeping Arden safe from other dangers. Their employer, Sinclair, trusts them implicitly with keeping the tavern safe, and knows all about their shady past. What that shady past is depends on you, whether it’s a previous smuggling job, previously from another city, or humbler origins in Arden.

[h3]Lord of Edges[/h3]

The Rogue may primarily serve as a damage class, but don’t let that fool you—they can also be a reliable tank with their Shroud ability!

Shroud allows the Rogue to envelop themselves in shadow, allowing them to automatically dodge any damage source once, as well as deal extra damage when active. However, you’ll lose Shroud if you’re hit by any source of damage, so try to avoid that. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/bfa14812a83bd914a491c0409c92fbfa97b85a4a.jpg[/img]
[i]It doesn’t go away with dealing damage though! Let your knives go brrrrr. [/i]

Movement is key to a Rogue, as you can’t be adjacent to enemies in order for your Shroud to activate. Some abilities will remove Shroud automatically when you deal damage to grant buffs or debuffs, such as their Sneak Attack ability, which Stuns the enemy after attacking but removes your beloved shadow cloak. 

To help the Rogue get the upper-hand (and perhaps set up some backstabbing shenanigans) they receive the following Skill Cards after the tutorial section:

[list]
[*] [b]Slice Twice:[/b] Move, hit an enemy twice, then move away or push them to get your Shroud ability. Best of all, Shroud gives you extra damage on that second hit! 
[*] [b]Isolate:[/b] Get more movement to find the perfect prey, then deal damage. You deal extra damage if that enemy has no one adjacent to them! 
[*] [b]Myriad Blades:[/b] Become an agent of the shadows by attacking, teleporting, and attacking again. Your enemies will never know what hit them. 
[/list]

Balancing between being in the enemy’s face and moving away to activate Shroud is key to a Rogue, but there are always options to get right back in their face! Using the right Skill Cards can have you dancing between enemies and tanking for your friends without a care in the world. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/91cf28d179388beafed09f5e7c4c30362e149d63.jpg[/img]
[i]Or, you know, to get loot. Priorities.[/i]

Once Rogues gain more experience, they’ll be able to add powerful Skill Cards into their arsenal, such as:
 
[list]
[*] [b]Pennypinch:[/b] An ability for your sticky fingers! Move, then attack, which creates gold, attack, create more gold, then move!  
[*] [b]Smoke and Mirrors:[/b] You thought the Arcanist made the only decoys? Attack, teleport away, and leave a decoy in your place. They’ll even attack the enemy after you move! 
[*] [b]Soulthieve: [/b]Move, then target an adjacent creature with buffs. Steal those for yourself, then deal damage with your new buffs! The more you stole, the more damage you deal!
[/list]

Of course, taking damage and dealing it back isn’t all the Rogue can do! With some key abilities, they’ll be able to heavily debuff enemies with Blind, Stun, and even Execute enemies! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/351ab7a78074ba64ab5bf15aee58a7ab37c51dc5.jpg[/img]
[i]This is the most front-facing damage a Rogue has ever done. [/i]

[h3]Shadowy Fate[/h3]

As the Rogue grows, so do your Fate Card options! While a ton of Fate Cards will help buff the Rogue, there are just as many that focus on survivability and sneakiness! 

The Rogue can use Fate Cards to turn their builds into:
[list]
[*] [b]Move and Stab:[/b] Give yourself extra Move to get Sneak attack back, or go for a new target mid-turn! 
[*] [b]Decoy Diversion: [/b]Create Decoys in your place to confuse enemies or have them attack your foes! 
[*] [b]Your Buffs Are My Buffs:[/b] Steal enemy buffs for yourself! They won’t need them anyways. 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/3618058d06222e28209498bfb8514842a914cd89.jpg[/img]
[i]The pit dilemma: Do you push them off a cliff, or stab them to show them who’s boss? [/i]

[h3]Ultimate Backstab[/h3]

The Rogue’s Ultimate Ability, Thousand Cuts, lives up to its name and then some. 

This ability grants the Rogue a Teleport next to an unwilling victim, then deals damage! If they’re under 8 health after the damage is dealt, they’ll automatically be Executed. If they are defeated, you can repeat the entire Ability again. Wheeee! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/ac9ae0aa514f740c2d0b820ecb0597a870a10f68.jpg[/img]
[i]He’s coming to GET YOU. [/i]

And that’s a wrap on the Sunderfolk Heroes! 

Next on our agenda is a deeper focus into the combat systems of Sunderfolk, as well as some exciting talks straight from our developers. Stay tuned! 

-- The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Meet Your Heroes: The Ranger
notes.content:
[h2]Markhor Marker[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/72533002326ccb9b34f9be543fd1288360dc9def.png[/img]

[i]It’s been great having ya living with me and the kid, and now everyone’ll see how great ya are too![/i] - Batu, the town clothier. 

The Ranger is a new addition to the town of Arden, taken in by Batu. The Ranger now devotes themselves to protecting their new home with their powerful ranged abilities. When playing, your Ranger may be focused on hunting, recovering from a devastating loss, or a traveling soul. No matter what you choose as their background, the Ranger will always be the party’s supportive archer. 

[h3]Underground Strider[/h3]
The Ranger is a perfect mix of damage and support, with focuses on ranged combat, debuffing enemies, and providing crowd control abilities. Their main source of damage comes from their passive, [b]Precision[/b], which lets you deal more damage when the range requirement is met and inflicts a debuff. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/2f68c797fdee7ccdaa789568bd81c5bdf84c3a76.jpg[/img]
[i]Expose increases damage taken by +1, and that includes environmental damage! [/i]

After completing the first series of missions, the Ranger will be able to use: 
[list]
[*] [b]Hunter’s Shot[/b] - Fire an arrow straight at the enemy. As straightforward as their arrow. 
[*] [b]Nock Back [/b]- Move, then push an enemy or ally back 3 hexes, then move again. Leaves Vines that can Root enemies or allow extra movement for allies. 
[*] [b]Piercing Arrow[/b] - A line attack that lets the Ranger move into position, and fire up to 5 hexes away. 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/2e6e65cb7a114a3a3dbc4c185e8bce2d3ab09de2.jpg[/img]
[i]Satisfying? Yes. Does it take a while to set up? Also yes. [/i]

A Ranger is at their best when they’re away from enemies, but they can also buff themselves and leap away if they need to get in close. Their [b]Spring Step [/b]skill allows you to attack, [b]Slow [/b]their enemy, then [b]Leap [/b]away to safety! If you land away from any monsters, you gain [b]Haste [/b]and [b]Strength[/b]! 

They also have light repositioning abilities that can not only be used to push away enemies, but can help you give your allies the needed push to get right into position and deal more damage! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/6794892555494f93eeceb9cd2aa767241fa84656.jpg[/img]
[i]Give your allies a healthy push in the right direction. [/i]

To add even more variety in their spells, the Ranger will also receive the following Skill Cards at higher levels: 
[list]
[*] [b]Scout Ahead [/b]- Attack, Move, then debuff up to 2 enemies with Expose! Your Rogue and Pyromancer friends will thank you.
[*] [b]Snaring Vines[/b] - Move, then create 3 Vines within 3 hexes of your location, then move again. Bait enemies into getting rooted, or help allies get to safety! 
[*] [b]Wild Bloom[/b] - You don’t need rain for this super bloom! Unleash an area-of-effect attack, and create 2 Vines in any empty hexes within the affected area, then move! 
[/list]

[h3]Piercing Fate[/h3]

Similar to the other heroes, early-game Fate Cards provided for the Ranger focus on either self-buffs or debuffs, so you can choose to build your Ranger as more damage-focused or support-focused! 

Potential builds for mid to late-game Rangers can be:
[list]
[*] [b]Debuff Hero[/b]: Anything and everything debuffs your foes. Draw an unlucky -2? Debuff. Grabbed a +1 but the enemy is still up? Debuffed for the next round. 
[*] [b]Leap and Vine[/b]: Need to get away but want to leave a mark? Pick Fate Cards that grant you Leap but leave a Vine in the exited hex. Your enemies couldn’t pursue you if they tried. 
[*] [b]Ranged is Good[/b]: Perfected the art of staying away from enemies? Use Fate Cards that buff your damage on top of your passive as long as you’re within the required range! Now that’s leaving your mark. 
[/list]

Either way, keep your distance from enemies and you’ll be the hero of your party for the amount of versatility you bring to the table. 

[b]Ultimate 360 No-Scope[/b]

Once they hit Level 6, the Ranger gets their ultimate Ability: [b]Snipe[/b].  

Snipe grants the Ranger 3 hexes of Move, then unleashes a powerful single-target attack that can be increased if the Ranger has any Strength buffs, and stacks with your passive ability. That’s one way to erase an enemy off the map. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/baa486be859539465a6912db7d24a6948011cf0a.png[/img]
[i]Hit them so hard they report you for hacking. [/i]

If ranged damage seems too safe and careful for you, then we can’t wait to introduce our next character! 

Up next is the Rogue spotlight! 

If you’d like to visit one of our earlier Hero spotlights, check out:
[list]
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2414270/view/501690949084119041]The Arcanist[/url]
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2414270/view/737004219196768260]The Bard[/url]
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2414270/view/521957873571332263]The Berserker [/url]
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2414270/view/536595207289832006]The Pyromancer[/url]
[/list]


Thank you!
The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Meet Your Heroes: The Pyromancer
notes.content:
[h2]Amphibian Conflagration [/h2] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/ccea89240e444910468429c9d0f19e4ba54c1df5.png[/img]

[i]“Now you’re actually doing something you might do well; setting things on fire! But for Arden this time!”[/i] - Scorch 

While their sibling Scorch might not be the brightest ember in the furnace, they do know one thing: their little kin has a mighty fire burning within them. The Pyromancer has always had a reputation to strive for, and based on your preferences, their dreams may lie within being a leader of the people, finding purpose after a long slumber, or perhaps failed ambition will drive them. 

No matter how you choose their path, they will always be the warmth that their party relies on. 

[h3]Pyrotactics[/h3]

The Pyromancer might look adorable, but they’re a confined inferno and they need to let it out.  Fire’s the name of the game, and unleashing it is the prize. The Pyromancer really gets their power by absorbing Fire and making it their own, then unleashing it through their skills. 

Each stack of Firepower, their passive ability, gives +2 to each attack, and they can stack it up to 3 times! This will also stack with any Strength buffs, so if you want to erase something off the map (with fire), the Pyromancer is for you. 

After completing the first few missions in Sunderfolk, the Pyromancer will be able to use: 
[list]
[*] [b]Bouncing Blaze:[/b] Move, deal ranged damage, with a bonus of your fireball bouncing to an adjacent enemy. It’s a deadly hot potato! 
[*][b] Flame Breath:[/b] Move towards enemies and unleash a line fire attack that can hit up to 3 foes! 
[*] [b]Meteor Crash:[/b] Become the fireball of your dreams. Leap 3, and deal damage to all enemies around your landing spot. You can also create your own Fire this way! 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/87f1d10ccad6929e05614861fd5ee489cac225bf.png[/img]
[i]Fun Fact: The Pyro loves being surrounded by fire! Not fun for your teammates, though. [/i]

The Pyromancer isn’t always just about raw damage! This is a game of strategy and tactics after all, and they’ll need to have a few extra tricks up their sleeve if they want to help their team out. Luckily, they do receive some great abilities that can help boost their survivability and overall tankiness. 

The Pyro can start to use the following Skill Cards at later levels: 
[list]
[*] [b]Trailblaze:[/b] Become the fiery change you want to be in the world. Set 3 hexes on fire, leap to one of them, then deal damage to whoever is in range. 
[*] [b]Cauterize:[/b] Did the Rogue take that last heal shrine? Move towards fire, choose an area with tons of it, then absorb it all and heal 2 health for each fire you absorb. Your teammates will appreciate the space back, too. 
[*] [b]Friendly Fire: [/b]Make your friends nervous by targeting them after moving, then unleash some fire right on them and deal damage to adjacent enemies! Your friend won’t be hurt, physically at least. 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/3fc711eaecbb42ec20205f0d95e7c0b2ff06b30f.jpg[/img]
[i]Look at that delighted face. No Rangers were harmed in the making of this screenshot. Well, not by the Pyro, anyway. [/i]

[h3]Fiery Fate[/h3]
What the Pyromancer makes up for in damage, they lose in mobility in early game missions.  However, you can eventually change that with the power of fate (cards)! 

You can either go the more damage route, or pick Skill Cards that can teleport you safety from danger. After all, enemies are going to want to hit the squishy salamander that made their friends go boom. 

Some Fate Card build options for the Pyro are:
[list]
[*] [b]Leaping Away: [/b]Using Leap cards can be a massive help when you’re surrounded by enemies. With some built-in leap cards, you can truly become the frog salamander-hop master. 
[*] [b]Absorb and Conquer:[/b] Using Fate Cards that allow you to absorb any adjacent Fire surrounding you is a great way to guarantee you’ll never run out of firepower. This also includes potential healing for any fire absorbed! 
[*] [b]All the Fire:[/b] Why wait for Fire to appear when you can make it yourself. With each cast, you’ll be able to add more Fire to the board, which can set up some defenses as well as leave you with plenty of fire to absorb later. 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/e01eeb6d2640b5289ffe49682d89591c7fdf4642.jpg[/img]
[i]Pair these Fate Cards with Meteor Strike, and you can leap frog your way across the map. If you’re lucky on the draw. [/i]

[h3]Ultimate Fireball[/h3]
The Pyromancer is no stranger to tons of damage, and their Ultimate ability, Inferno, truly embodies that sentiment. Inferno allows the Pyromancer to dominate the field by moving into position, and cast a massive area-of-effect fireball that damages enemies and leaves behind a roaring fire in each empty hex that the fireball hits. 

So if there ARE enemies left after that, they’ll be surrounded by, well, you know. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/3373d78dd1e842e7bd0547dde6ac807ff364a97e.png[/img]
[i]A dexterity save won’t save you from this! [/i]

While the Pyromancer is hard to top when it comes to dealing damage, they’re hardly a one-man show. If you want a good mix of support and long-range attacks, then we have the perfect character for you!

Stay tuned for the Ranger spotlight! 

If you’d like to visit one of our earlier Hero spotlights, check out:
[list]
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2414270/view/501690949084119041]The Arcanist[/url]
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2414270/view/737004219196768260]The Bard[/url]
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2414270/view/521957873571332263]The Berserker [/url]
[/list]

Thank you! 

- The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Meet Your Heroes: The Berserker
notes.content:
[h2]Bear-rier from Pain[/h2] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/e658120d27b7d605b9acf0b1d8da83603137e186.png[/img]

[i]“Benefits of growing up with you: Ogres don’t seem so scary.” [/i]- Bramble, the Berserker’s sibling. 

The Berserker has always been the reliable go-to animal for their younger sibling Bramble, and they continue that tradition by being a guardian of Arden. Your Berserker may have picked up a sweeter trade prior to their hero duties, be retired from their previous position as gate guard, or a travelling protector, but one thing is always clear—they always protect their fellow Sunderfolk. 

[h3]Load-Bearer[/h3]

While the Berserker may seem no more than a simple tank at first glance, their wide array of combat abilities—paired with their staggering selection of self buffs—allows them to roar in the face of danger (sometimes literally!). 

Their passive is Protector’s Fury, which makes the Berserker take less damage and deal more damage as long it’s active. It’s not only effective against enemy attacks, but will also work for any external damage, such as environmental tiles like lava and fire. The only catch is that you need to be HIT first before it activates… so get in there and get mad! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/1260276a2cf515a0500bcb3c20c6f92c7e8c75a6.jpg[/img]
[i]Are they ever really in danger, though? [/i]

Once you clear the first set of missions, the Berserker has three main Skill Cards: 
[list]
[*] [b]Bulwark:[/b] The tried and true tank ability. Move to position, then deal a nasty swing that provokes the enemy hit and gives the Berserker a shield. 
[*] [b]Fling:[/b] Your best friend if there’s a pit involved. Move, grab an enemy (or a friend!) and [strike]yeet them aggressively [/strike]throw them where you think they should be. 
[*] [b]Whirlwind:[/b] Surrounded by enemies? Good! Want to be surrounded by them? Move yourself and let loose your hammer to hit all enemies around you. 
[/list]

The Berserker has little to no regard for personal boundaries and loves to get right up in the face of whoever might be in their way.. They’re an absolute unit of a Guardian, though, and that means reduced movement—which can sometimes hinder them from getting where they want (or need) to be. That’s why the Berserker also comes equipped with abilities that grant them lots of Move, like Bring It On, as well as ones that brings enemies to THEM.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/ea232d79513472225e06d48bf29b16c82d988d56.jpg[/img]
[i]If you don’t shout “GET OVER HERE” while using Long Haul, you get -1 coolness. We don’t make the rules, we just let you know. [/i]

The Berserker may seem less complex than some of our other playable characters, but that simplicity is only fur-deep. As they level up, the Berserker will unlock a wide range of abilities that make them one of the most fearsome creatures on the map, including: 

[list]
[*] [b]Grisly Force: [/b]Move towards enemies, then deal 3 damage to yourself. Sounds grisly, but then ALL damage you’ve taken adds to the final damage you deal to the enemy. 
[*] [b]Take Down: [/b]Thought the Berserker wasn’t scary enough before? Attack, then follow with a Move and another attack! Best of all, if you take down an enemy with the first attack, you’ll get a strength buff AND a shield! 
[*] [b]Hibernate: [/b]Need to heal in a pinch? Move away from the scary things, shield yourself, then use your Rage to heal. You get extra health if you use this card with less than five health remaining. 
[/list]

That’s just a taste of the Berserker’s rage, and they only get meaner as they grow stronger! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/da88249c668ef085256fb6048057e8ef1f5c76a9.jpg[/img]
[i]Provoke ensures the enemy attacks you on their next turn. You made them mad! [/i]

[h3]Provoking Fate[/h3]

Like their fellow party members, the Berserker’s Fate Deck starts out simple, primarily focused on Strength and Shield buffs. However, as they level up, the amount of build options available to them through careful card selection growls grows! 

Fate Cards that grant Haste, Shield, or Strength are always good for early game Berserkers. For mid-game? Keep an eye out for cards that focus on crowd control so you don’t have to rely solely on abilities like Bulwark. 

As you progress, you’ll unlock Fate Cards with buffs like Retaliate! Or, you can stack your Fate Deck with nothing but Strength buffs, allowing you to transform your Berserker from a tanky bear into a… regular, scary bear. 

Some Fate Card builds for the Berserker can be: 
[list]
[*] [b]Bear [strike]Totem [/strike]Tank:[/b] Become a true defense character. Stack Shields, Retaliate, and Heal cards so even your -2 Cards help you survive. 
[*] [b]Charging Forth:[/b] Feel like your Berserker isn’t moving enough? Stack Charge buffs which let you move outside of your normal ability Moves and deal damage while moving. 
[*] [b]Provoke, Throw, Repeat:[/b] Become a frustrating (for your enemies) combination of a taunting tank who makes enemies walk BACK to them for some more punishment. 
[/list]

[h3]Ultimate Roar[/h3]

Starting at Level 6, the Berserker gets their ultimate Ability: Roar! 

This ability gives them 3 hexes of Move, followed by a devastating area-of-effect damage blow coupled with a debuff to them, then finally shields each hero and ally nearby. It’s a war cry and massive attack in one fell blow! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/8adbf8fb4dad356d3c2883dd6eaca16ae1093114.png[/img]
[i]You… made them mad. You really didn’t want to make them mad. [/i]

However, if you want to leave damage to the professionals, might we suggest their fiery friend? 

More on the Pyromancer soon! 

If you missed one of our earlier Hero spotlights, check out:
[list]
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2414270/view/501690949084119041]The Arcanist [/url]
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2414270/view/737004219196768260]The Bard[/url]
[/list]

Thank you!

The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Meet Your Heroes: The Bard
notes.content:
[h2]Classical Chiroptera[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/184fb74da49ead5ab80c6f4672fa43511a89d7e1.png[/img]

[i]“You played the most beautiful tune I’d ever heard! I knew then…that you were spending far too much time on recreation!”[/i] - Sentinel Treak 

Despite the best efforts of their adoptive guardian, Sentinel Treak (who’d much rather the Bard be a dedicated soldier, discipline above all!), the Bard devotes themselves to their craft and to protecting Arden. They were either exiled, a prodigal talent, or trained for other specialties, but how their ballad in Sunderfolk is crafted depends on you!

[h3]The Beat of Combat[/h3]

Using the power of music, the Bard focuses on map manipulation as well as supportive buffs to make their team shine. Their passive, Two-Step, can really help a melee teammate close the distance, or allow for quick and easy buffs right before getting into attack mode. 

You can drop their Music Notes by swapping positions (as long as Two-Step is available), using certain abilities, or utilizing select trinkets and weapons to fill the battlefield with buffs. However, those can be trampled by enemies, so choose your positioning carefully!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/a876959cf94e76500e3294950a2f9a6c702dde8a.jpg[/img]
[i]A trait so good, it becomes a powerful spell mid-game! Be the rockstar of your dreams. [/i]

Once you’ve completed the tutorial missions, you’ll have the following Skill Cards in your repertoire: 

[list]
[*] [b]Sharp Refrain:[/b] Move, deal single-target damage, then summon a Music Note next to the enemy you hit. 
[*] [b]Siren Song: [/b]Move, enchant a friend or foe to walk towards you, then move yourself again! 
[*] [b]Beat Drop:[/b] Leap right into the fray, push enemies away, then strut away in style. 
[/list]

Controlling the map is truly their specialty, though, with abilities that can move either allies or enemies, depending on the situation! While their ability Siren Song is picked up right at the beginning of the game, being able to position allies or enemies for setups gives it longevity that’s truly unmatched.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/102b8a9257e6006890c3ba5f67910b4cb6fcc465.jpg[/img]
[i]Damage, crowd control, AND drops buffs? What CAN’T music solve?[/i]

To complement their early board-blocking and bestie-boosting beats, the Bard will also receive the following abilities at higher levels: 

[list]
[*] [b]Shield Sonata: [/b]Hit an enemy, shield whichever ally was next to that enemy, then walk towards friends and shield them again! 
[*] [b]Power Chord:[/b] Deal damage to enemies around you, push them away, then buff your allies with some Strength! 
[*] [b]Crowd Surf: [/b]The best movement and repositioning spell, use your Two-Step passive to great effect then deal damage based on how much you moved! 
[/list]

Of course, you’ll get even more abilities as you level up and get stronger! And, with a clever selection of trinkets and/or weapons, you might even leave the Arcanist weeping in jealousy of your ability to manipulate your surroundings. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/65d0ecea30db32770e97225fad2c4374b1f5b430.jpg[/img]
[i]Use your powers wisely! [/i]

[h3]Playing With Fate[/h3]

Just like all of our playable characters in Sunderfolk, The Bard’s Fate Deck will begin with the standard suite of cards that affect their attack damage output. 

As they level up, more nuanced Fate Cards will appear! Many of these cards will provide the Bard self-buffs, so that they can stay alive even if they've beat-dropped themselves into a sticky situation, while others may kick off a buff-et for your friends to feast on! 

The Bard can use Fate Cards to turn their builds into:

[list]
[*] [b]ALL of the Music Notes: [/b] Deal -2 to your roll? Get some Music Notes. Extra Move on a Neutral card?  You guessed it, Music Notes to accompany your small journey. 
[*] [b]Vicious Enemy Mockery:[/b] Become the debuff champion and make enemies regret even targeting you. 
[*] [b]Inspire and Revive:[/b] Want to Inspire your allies to attack enemies near them, without moving or using an ability card? Your Fate Decks can help! You can also set Fate Cards to Heal allies! All it takes is a lucky draw. 
[/list]

[h3]Ultimate Performance[/h3]

Their Ultimate Ability, Mosh Pit, is the grand finale to the Bard’s kit once they reach level 6. 
This ability gives the Bard five spaces of movement then deals area-of-effect damage to nearby enemies. But that’s not all! It also enchants all fellow party members, compelling them to move towards the Bard and attack any enemies within range after reaching their destination. It’s so punk rock.🤘! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/31917c6d2f986c3aa43113aa08cba49e719081be.png[/img]
[i]The power of music compels you! [/i]

No matter how good the Bard may be with positioning and support, they still can’t tank ALL of the damage…which leads to our next deep dive: the Berserker!

Stay tuned for more info on our beefy ursine guardian! 

- The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Meet Your Heroes: The Arcanist
notes.content:
[h2]Corvid Conjuries[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/4069e5996e0c878a844d381eee6312db43e89f08.png[/img]

[i]“I’ll be the first to admit it; your magic is super bright!” [/i] - Kazera

Much to the slight annoyance of their roommate, the oracle Kazera, the Arcanist has a powerful ability to manipulate magic around them. Your Arcanist can be reclusive, from a shady background, or be one to spot malicious intent from a mile away! 

[h3]Abilities, Mana, And You[/h3]
This corvid conjurer focuses on casting abilities using Mana, a resource that is acquired both passively and through select abilities. Their most powerful spells are locked behind a higher Mana cost, but what those spells lose in early Round availability they make up for in sheer utility and damage. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/41b583a8b667a8273a8cd6d07206a39e8c4c8ef4.jpg[/img]
[i]Case in point, pull them in and deal ALL OF THE DAMAGE. [/i]

After finishing all the tutorial encounters, you’ll start the game with three Skill Cards:

[list]
[*] [b]Thunderclap: [/b]Move, deal single-target damage, then Push an enemy away. 
[*] [b]Stargate: [/b]Teleport to a desired location, then Swap a character to another location. If there’s someone already there, they’ll swap places!
[*][b] Gravity Nexus: [/b]Move, pull in all enemies within 3 hexes, then deal area-of-effect damage around the Arcanist. Then teleport to safety! 
[/list]

You'll also gain an extra Skill Card that will always be available in your deck: Mana Spring. This ability allows you to regain a large amount of Mana based on how many characters are adjacent to you at the time of its use -- including enemies!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/d124cbb0a4d860c275a9ea19663962c5a504259f.jpg[/img]
[i]Use your allies (and enemies) positions for your benefit. For mana. Manafit. [/i]

A true scholar of the arcane arts, the Arcanist usually has a spell for every situation. And, as you level up, you'll unlock a variety of complex and interesting abilities like:
[list]
[*] [b]Aetherize: [/b]An ability with a high Mana cost, but powerful single-target damage.
[*] [b]Mirror Shatter:[/b] Oops too many decoys? Sacrifice them for even more damage. 
[*] [b]Chaos Beam:[/b] Rewrite reality itself (within a line attack, at least).
[/list]

Even more spells await you in-game, so if you’re interested in some hijinks, make sure to slot the Arcanist in your party! 

[h3]Fate Decks[/h3]

Fate Cards are a core part of gameplay in Sunderfolk.

We'll be digging into this mechanic more in the future -- but, for now, just know that when a character performs an ability that includes an attack, they will draw a Fate Card from their Fate Deck. Based on the Fate Card that's drawn, that attack will then be augmented in some way.

Every character starts with a basic collection of Positive, Neutral, and Negative Fate cards that will impact the final damage output of their attacks. As you progress through the campaign, you’ll gain more and more Fate Cards, including ones that allow you to customize your character's build in fun and exciting ways.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/c69756436dc72f74161bec2d897cad4fdae27edd.png[/img]
[i]Early level Fate Cards keep it simple, but as the game (and your knowledge) grows, so does the build customization! Neat![/i]

For the Arcanist, some of these build options might focus on survivability, extra damage, debuffing enemies, or utilizing your unique spells – like spawning extra Decoys, for example. (Normally, you can only spawn Decoys by using a specific ability card. With this Fate Card, however, EVERY ability now has that chance, changing up your entire strategy.)

The Arcanist is truly a jack-of-all-trades when it comes to customizing their playstyle. 
[list]
[*] [b]Want more damage for those sweet high-mana cost abilities? [/b]Give yourself Fate Cards that add Strength buffs for future setups. 
[*] [b]Want to outdo the support characters with debuffs? [/b]Stack your deck with Fate Cards to Debuff ALL THE THINGS and set up for the ultimate KO. 
[*] [b]Don’t want to use your precious turn to use Mana Spring for more Mana? [/b]Add more Fate Cards that refund or add Mana to your deck with a lucky draw. 
[/list]

With some careful planning, you can make even the Negative Fate Cards work for your strategies. 

[h3]Ultimate Power[/h3]

In Sunderfolk, characters unlock their Ultimate ability at Level 6 (once they've theoretically learned enough responsibility to manage it). These abilities are powerful and can be game-changing, depending on how you play. However, there's a catch! Each Ultimate has a cooldown, and only one Ultimate can be used per Round. This means communication is key -- you'll need to strategize with your fellow members to determine which character should use their Ultimate...and when!

In the case of the Arcanist, their Ultimate is Starfall. This area-of-effect spell packs a mean one-two punch, applying a Confusion debuff to every target it hits as well as stunning whatever enemy is at the center of its radius. (Note: Not only does Confusion cause affected creatures to potentially hit their friends, but it also makes you look REALLY cool when casting it.)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/815b5cde6b47b5464c3a26d649a35a03af49fc44.jpg[/img]
[i]If you can’t get stars from the heavens, store-bought is fine. [/i]

Speaking of stars… 

Up next in our “Meet the Hero” series is…the beat-dropping Bard!

- The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: The World of Sunderfolk Awaits!
notes.content:
[h2] Enter the Sunderlands [/h2]

Illuminated by the Life Tree and brightstone crystal at its core, the town of Arden has been spared the chaos that envelops the surrounding Sunderlands. Its denizens have trusted the stone's protective glow to keep their paths lit and hearts warm for generations, but something now stirs in the looming dark...and their peace may not last forever.

Here is where your story begins, the story of the Guardians of the community of Arden. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/0b802c8ae0e41d134090b2b9d88a724a4201482c.png[/img][i]The town of Arden, illuminated by the Life Tree, intertwined with the Brightshard. [/i]

[h2 ]The Basics [/h2]

Upon starting Sunderfolk, you’ll be able to choose from one of six characters, all with unique playstyles that neatly fit into their own specialities. From the buff-granting, tune-slinging Bard to the kill-all-things-with-fire Pyromancer, your characters will be your connection to the world, so choose your preferred approach and get ready to help save your beloved home. 

You’ll begin your new campaign as fresh-faced adventurers, recently back from an incursion and ready to sit down and unwind . . . but things never happen how you’d like them to, do they?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/4993affeb5cb24204ab3942ebdf083f496e0169e.jpg[/img]
[i]Behold, (some of) your heroes. More on all of them soon! [/i]

As you level up, you'll collect and even forge your own new equipment to stave off the shadow from your town." Utilizing trinkets, weapons, and your own arsenal of skills will help you face any challenge thrown at you . . . and sometimes even throw it back! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/d10e347d21499ef950277d28f49118578470845f.png[/img]
[i]Using Fling increases your cool factor by 1000%. Yes, we checked. [/i]

You’ll also get to know the residents of Arden, how they’re connected with you and each other, and forge relationships that will help—or hinder—your time in the Sunderlands. The villagers  of Arden are very personable, so don’t be afraid to talk to them while you’re in town in between missions to purchase items, upgrade your weapons and trinkets, or just get to know all of their lovely personalities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/1f6588d286c331b6ba639d3f17fe9a37a3fa83f4.jpg[/img]
[i]All you need to know is Chirp is here, and Chirp is the best. Don’t @ us. [/i]

[h2] Playing Sunderfolk [/h2]

Controlling this game is a bit different than your standard strategy-focused game! Sunderfolk utilizes mobile devices (phones and tablets)  as a new way to play and display information. This covers everything from:
[list]
* Movement in combat 
* Using your ability cards
* What your mission rules and objectives are
* Hero information
* Even what your enemies can whip up! 
[/list]

It’s like having your controller hold your character sheet and game guide, all in one convenient package. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/f39288f9703464d8360d07de95d782e9cfdb9c3e.jpg[/img]
[i]Phone not included in Sunderfolk purchase.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/27e4c07e31415f396fbc93211230f370041f83bb.png[/img]
[i]Oh yeah, did we mention you can name some monsters? [/i]

[h2] New Difficulty Approaches [/h2]

Need a little challenge in your life? 

Well, once you’ve mastered the basics, or even right off the bat, you can set your preferred difficulty level in Sunderfolk to Challenging. This setting introduces Round Limits, which places a cap on how many total turns you and your fellow party members have to complete a specific mission before it fails.  It also decreases your total number of available Life Seeds (pictured in the upper right hand corner of the screenshot below), reducing the number of times your characters can be automatically revived.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/420d68f737d4f27bf403c249e30531e51771f556.png[/img]
[i]Yes, it DID feel good to get that lined up, thanks for asking. We did fail that mission, though. [/i]

Sunderfolk is designed to be played as an ongoing campaign, with an overarching story and the same characters chosen at select for the entire game. You and your friends can easily set the game down and return weekly to begin your new escapades into the Sunderlands, or create a new campaign with new characters with a different setup. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45246535/0304d8e327b2c37e137fe1e0677057b325ab3364.jpg[/img]
[i]Be the talk of the town with your incredible barrel movement. [/i]

And that's just the tip of the Sunderberg. 

We'll be digging into the details of our character classes, combat mechanics, town hub systems, music, art, NPCs, and so much more. So, stay tuned!

-- The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Join us in the Sunderfolk Steam Beta!
notes.content:
[h1] The Sunderfolk Closed Beta [/h1]

Our Closed Beta has been ongoing since December 11, 2024, but we’d love to get more insights before it officially ends on [b] February 4th, 2025! [/b]

That’s why we want our Steam community to join us and give us your thoughts! The best way to see if something works is to try it out, and we need your insights to make sure Sunderfolk delivers our team’s vision—a new way to play board games and introduce loved ones into this amazing genre. 

[h2] How to Participate [/h2] 

Here are the steps you need to follow:

[b]Step 1:[/b] [url=https://sflk.gg/beta] Sign-up for our Sunderfolk Closed Beta [/url]

[b]Step 2:[/b] [url=https://hs.dreamhaven.com/dh-account-how-to] Create a Dreamhaven account [/url]

[b]Step 3:[/b] [url=https://hs.dreamhaven.com/dh-account-steam-how-to]Link your Steam, PlayStation, and/or Xbox accounts [/url]

[b]Step 4:[/b] [url=https://hs.dreamhaven.com/dh-account-discord-how-to]Link your Discord account [/url]

Since this closed beta is under NDA, if you’re accepted into this limited test, you’ll be asked to join our Closed Beta Discord server where you can chat with your fellow Sundertesters and provide all the feedback in one convenient location! 

We'll be sending out invites beginning [b] January 24th, 2025 [/b]! 

This is still a limited closed beta, so we may not be able to invite everyone, but we are looking to get more Steam users to join us!

[i]Don’t worry, if you’d like to play on a supported platform other than Steam, you can! Simply choose your desired platform when signing up.[/i]

If you’re accepted, you’ll receive full download instructions along with your beta key when you get your invitation. We’ll see you in Arden soon! 

[h2] Sunderfolk Closed Beta FAQ [/h2]

[b]Will I be able to post about the closed beta on my social media? [/b]
[list]
[*] No—anyone who plays during this playtest period will be subject to an NDA and will not be able to share any information about the game during this phase. 
[/list]
[b]How long will the closed beta last?[/b]
[list]
[*] The closed beta will end on February 4, 2025. 
[/list]
[b]How do I know if I was accepted?[/b]
[list]
[*] We’ll be sending you an email with more information about the beta if you get selected. Please make sure to sign up!
[/list]
[b]On what platforms will the closed beta be on?[/b]
[list]
[*] This beta test will be available on Steam, PlayStation®5, and Xbox Series X|S
[/list]
[b]Will my campaign be carried over to launch? [/b]
[list]
[*] No, while you’ll be able to play as many campaigns as you’d like during the test, all data will be reset upon the conclusion of the beta test. 
[/list]
[b]Would I be able to play solo instead of a group, or pick up for a missing friend that week?[/b]
[list]
[*] Yes! You will be able to play up to four characters at once as a single player, or take control of an existing character in someone else’s campaign. Simply click on the “+” plus sign on the top left corner where your round character portrait is, and select the empty character. If you intend to run a solo playthrough, you’ll be able to select your four characters by repeatedly using the + sign until all are selected. 
[/list]
[b]In what regions will the closed beta be available? [/b]
[list]
[*] The closed beta will be available to players in the US and Europe. 
[/list]
[b]What languages are supported? [/b]
[list]
[*] Only English will be supported during the beta; we plan on having multiple languages when the game launches. 
[/list]
[b]What do I need in order to play the game? [/b]
[list]
[*] You will need your PC (with an active Steam account) or preferred console (Xbox Series X|S or PlayStation 5) and either an Android or Apple mobile device to play. 
[/list]
[b]Can I invite my friends? [/b]
[list]
[*] Yes! Once you’re accepted, you will be able to play with up to three other players who do NOT need to be accepted into the beta test. However, please note that everything is confidential, and ALL players will be subject to the NDA. 
[/list]
[b]I can’t find my question?[/b]
[list]
[*] Oh no! Send it to us via [url=discord.gg/sunderfolk] Discord[/url], [url=twitter.com/sunderfolk] Twitter [/url], or player support (support@sunderfolk.com) and we will do our best to answer it! 
[/list]

Thank you,
The Sunderfolk Team

notes.title: Sunderfolk is a gorgeous new DnD style adventure from Blizzard's former boss
notes.content:
One of the holy grails in PC gaming has always been to accurately recreate the feeling of playing a tabletop RPG like Dungeons and Dragons. From titles like Baldur's Gate 3 and Planescape Torment to Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic and Wildermyth, there have been loads of games that have tilted a lance at the PC gaming TTRPG crown. One newly announced game from some ex-Blizzard veterans, titled Sunderfolk, will be joining their ranks and is looking to take that crown for itself.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Announcing Sunderfolk!
notes.content:
We’re so excited to finally announce Sunderfolk, the first game developed by Secret Door and published by Dreamhaven! 

This upcoming venture is designed for new and veteran fans of tabletop, board, and video games, and will be available on Steam, Playstation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch. 

Sunderfolk is a tactical couch co-op RPG created with one purpose, to bring new and veteran players together in a shared goal of tactics, survival, and triumph. 

You and three of your friends can pick one of six available classes; the Arcanist, Bard, Berserker, Pyromancer, Ranger, and Rogue, and begin a one-of-a-kind experience told through both your main screen and your phone, which acts as your main controller for the adventure. 

Each character has their own unique set of skills that encompass the essence of beloved character archetypes, so you’ll feel right at home for your preferred playstyle. 

Combat in Sunderfolk is always changing, as there is no set turn order to be bound by. There’s always a chance of changes to goals or enemy formations, so formulate plans on a whim, obsessively check encounter information, and work together with your friends to help Arden maintain their light against the ever-growing gloom.
